title: Akali Dal Chief Sukhbir Badal Meets PM Modi as Punjab Alliance Buzz Intensifies
excerpt: The meeting between the SAD president and the prime minister comes amid growing speculation of a BJP-Akali Dal reunion ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly elections.
body:
• Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, their most high-profile meeting since the SAD left the BJP-led NDA in 2020 over the farm laws.
  • The meeting has fueled speculation of a BJP-SAD alliance revival ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, with both parties separately signaling they are assessing all political options.
  • Badal was re-elected SAD president in April 2025 after surviving an assassination attempt in December 2024, and the party has recently attracted BJP defectors including Punjab BJP vice-president Arvind Khanna.
  • The political dynamics carry weight for the global Sikh diaspora, which closely tracks Punjab governance, religious affairs, and the treatment of Sikh community interests by New Delhi.

Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, a meeting that has set off a new wave of political speculation in Punjab and drawn close attention from the Sikh diaspora worldwide.

The meeting marks the most significant direct engagement between Badal and Modi since the Akali Dal severed its three-decade alliance with the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance in September 2020. The party had walked out over the central government's contentious agricultural reform laws, which triggered months of farmer protests concentrated heavily in Punjab.

A Thaw in Relations

Badal has made multiple visits to New Delhi in recent months, holding talks with senior BJP leaders. The meetings have intensified discussions about whether the two former allies will reunite before the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, where both parties face an Aam Aadmi Party government under Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.

BJP national president Nitin Nabin said recently that the party is "assessing all political scenarios" in Punjab, a statement widely interpreted as leaving the door open for a renewed alliance. BJP state general secretary Jagmohan Raju, meanwhile, confirmed the party would contest all 117 seats independently — but notably rejected only an alliance with the party of Khadur Sahib MP Amritpal Singh, not with the SAD.

Badal himself has not ruled out future cooperation. "Our focus is on strengthening our organization in Punjab," he said, without shutting down alliance speculation.

Badal's Political Resurrection

The meeting caps a turbulent period for the Akali Dal president. In November 2024, Badal resigned as party chief after the Akal Takht, the highest temporal authority in Sikhism, declared him "tankhaiya" — guilty of religious misconduct — for mistakes committed during the SAD's tenure in government. He was assigned "seva" (religious service) at the Golden Temple in Amritsar.

In December 2024, Badal survived an assassination attempt at the Golden Temple complex. By April 2025, he was re-elected party president with 524 delegates voting in his favor.

"The storm which will throw out Delhi parties from Punjab has started today."

— Sukhbir Badal, after Punjab BJP vice-president Arvind Khanna joined the Akali Dal

That confident tone has been bolstered by recent defections from the BJP to the SAD. Punjab BJP vice-president and two-time legislator Arvind Khanna joined the Akali Dal along with several BJP office-bearers, including a district president. Khanna described his move as a "homecoming" and praised Badal's relief work during the 2025 Punjab floods.

Punjab's Three-Way Fight

Punjab is currently governed by the AAP, which swept to power in 2022 on a wave of anti-incumbency against the BJP-SAD alliance and the Congress. But the party has faced growing criticism over paper leak scandals, with Badal accusing the AAP government of presiding over leaks in at least 10 recruitment exams.

The BJP, which has historically been a junior partner in Punjab, has been working to expand its footprint independently. The Congress, once dominant in the state, is attempting its own revival.

A revived BJP-SAD alliance would reshape this calculus, combining the BJP's organizational machinery and central government leverage with the Akali Dal's deep roots in rural and Sikh-majority constituencies.

Diaspora Stakes

The political trajectory in Punjab carries outsized significance for the global Sikh diaspora, particularly in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The community has closely watched New Delhi's handling of Sikh religious affairs, the Kartarpur Corridor, judicial representation — Badal has previously urged Modi to address the absence of Sikh judges in the Supreme Court — and more recently, the diplomatic fallout from the Khalistan-related incidents in Canada and the United States.

A Badal-Modi rapprochement would signal that mainstream Sikh political leadership is re-engaging with the BJP-led center, a development likely to be viewed through sharply different lenses across diaspora communities — some seeing pragmatic politics, others questioning whether Sikh interests will once again be subordinated to coalition arithmetic.

With 2027 approaching, the meeting between Badal and Modi may prove to be either a courtesy call or the opening move in a political realignment that reshapes Punjab's landscape for a decade.
nri_angle: The Badal-Modi meeting signals potential re-engagement between mainstream Sikh political leadership and the BJP center, a development the global Sikh diaspora will scrutinize through the lens of Punjab governance and community interests.
author: Diaspora Desk
